The race

President Trump, aboard Air Force One, 13 September 2026
The warnings
Alarm from inside the labs
Resigned

1,400
people working inside AI labs signed an open letter urging regulation, July 2026.

Beyond the Terminator
Risk runs along a spectrum
Quiet, latent
Loud, explicit
Beliefs
Biases and values embedded in the systems, unnoticed
The mind
How we learn, how we think, how we judge

Ask the room
Hands up if…
  1. You use AI: ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, anything
  2. Shout out: what do you use it for?
  3. You mostly trust what it tells you
  4. You use it to learn something new
  5. You’ve asked it about Islam: a ruling, a hadith
  6. You understand how it works under the hood
Artificial intelligence
But what is intelligence?
  • Taking in the world through the senses
  • Storing and recalling memory
  • Recognising patterns and relations
  • Reasoning from the seen to the unseen
  • Predicting; deriving the law of gravity
  • Weaving the senses into one understanding
أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
afalā taʿqilūn
Will you not use your reason?
Turing’s game
Can machines think?
1950
Alan Turing replaces the question with a game: can a machine pass for human in typed conversation?
73%
In 2025, GPT-4.5 was judged to be the human 73% of the time, more often than the real humans.
The twist: it won only after being told to make typos and seem less clever.
Source: Jones & Bergen, “Large Language Models Pass the Turing Test” (2025)
How AI works
“The cat sat on the …”
What comes next?
Next-word prediction
It learns probabilities over words
Everything it has read
The cat sat on the mat.
The cat sat on the mat.
The cat sat on the mat.
The cat sat on the mat.
The cat sat on the bat.
The cat sat on the cat.
What follows “the…”
mat
4 of 6 · 67%
bat
1 of 6 · 17%
cat
1 of 6 · 17%
Real models weigh the whole conversation, not just the last word. The principle is the same.
Training
The internet as teacher
Text
A vast share of the public internet, plus books and code
Patterns
Which words follow which, and how often
Structure
Grammar, facts, the shape of an argument
Reasoning?
Text that looks like reasoning, and increasingly is
It keeps the patterns, not the books.
So what’s the problem?
The internet is not humanity.
Overwhelmingly English
Disproportionately Western
Heavily recent
Tilted to whoever writes most
Rubbish, errors, and values it never states aloud: the model absorbs them all, then reasons from them.
Ask the room
“Two Muslims walked into a…”
How did the machine finish the sentence?
GPT-3, tested in 2021
It finished the sentence with violence
66/100
completions turned violent: shootings, bombings, killings
23%
of analogies mapped “Muslim” to “terrorist”
20%
still violent with kind words added: more than for any other religion tested
It was inventing, not recalling: new weapons, new settings, the same association.
Source: Abid, Farooqi & Zou, “Persistent Anti-Muslim Bias in Large Language Models” (Stanford & McMaster, 2021)
Implicit bias
A pattern no one chose
Nobody wrote “Muslims are violent” into the program.
The machine overheard it, from millions of sentences, each perhaps innocent on its own.
What they whispered together
Where the word “Muslim” appears, violence is usually nearby.
Today, the obvious bias has been corrected.
Corrected — by whom?
By what standard? Who decided what it should believe instead?
Tarbiyah
Learning a language is not being raised
Stage one · pre-training
Learning the language
Like a child absorbing words, patterns and grammar: “apple” points to a fruit.
Stage two · fine-tuning
The upbringing
Shaped to fit people’s manners, ethics and temperament: preference fine-tuning.
The same English, in London, Lahore or Texas, carries different values.
Preference fine-tuning
One choice, repeated millions of times
“What should I drink to unwind after a long day?”
Answer A
A glass of wine.
Answer B
Warm milk, or a walk.
A person picks one. The model is nudged towards it. Whichever the labellers prefer becomes the machine’s instinct.
Qiyās · reasoning by analogy
Same structure, different cause
Step
Sound qiyās
Unsound qiyās
Original case (aṣl)
Wine (khamr)
Wine
Ruling (ḥukm)
Forbidden, Qur’an 5:90
Forbidden
Effective cause (ʿillah)
Intoxication
Made from grapes
New case (farʿ)
Whisky
Fresh grape juice
Conclusion
Haram: sound
Haram: wrong ruling
The test: wine that turns to vinegar no longer intoxicates, and becomes lawful. The cause goes; the ruling goes with it.
Trained to please
“You’re absolutely right!”
2023 · Anthropic researchers show preference-trained models tell people what they want to hear
2025 · OpenAI withdraws a ChatGPT update for being too eager to please
And when another AI does the judging: who wrote the rules?
What a chatbot gave me
Narrated Abū Hurayrah: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “Whoever lights a lamp for a traveller in the darkness, Allah will light for him a path on the Day when there is no light but His.”
Recorded by al-Tirmidhī, who said: ḥasan gharīb.
A narrator, a collection, even a grading. I could not find it in any collection.
AI-generated · not a hadith
FABRICATED · NOT A HADITH
How it was made
Pattern without a chain
Authentic · Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī
Glad tidings of complete light on the Day of Resurrection, for those who walk to the mosque in darkness.
Fabricated · no source
A lamp for a traveller… a path on the Day when there is no light but His.
Plausibility wearing the clothes of truth.
Safety
When it teaches our children
Is it good pedagogy?
The methods it uses to teach
Is it thinking for them?
The long-term cost to how they learn
Is it always safe?
Never telling a child something harmful or untrue
Not hacking or warfare: a soft conditioning of the mind.
Judgement
Can we trust its judgement?
With a human in the loop
  • Lawyers working through legal documents
  • Accountants crunching numbers
  • Developers writing code
Faster and sharper
Left on its own
Decisions built on reasoning that is subtly wrong, and nobody checks.
Where the danger begins
A thought experiment
Resemblance is not a cause
The real cause
Better funding, smaller classes, experienced teachers
More computers
The AI’s conclusion: buy more
Better results
The link the AI saw
The grape juice mistake: wrong ʿillah, confident ruling, and real children on the other end.
Muslim responsibility
Who sits in the room where its conscience is written?
2
countries build the most capable systems: the United States and China
Everyone else, every nation, every faith, every community, is in effect spoken for.
What we can do
Three responsibilities
01
Our own data
Digitise, index and edit the tradition, so the machine can point to its source: an isnād.
02
Our own frameworks
Set out our values and uṣūl, to evaluate, govern and train. Scholars and engineers in one room.
03
Ownership
Chips, data centres, power: who owns and secures them is a question of sovereignty.
أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ

Who teaches the machine? Right now, mostly not us. It doesn’t have to stay that way.
